# WavEncoder

[DotGame.AudioCodecs](README.md) · `DotGame.AudioCodecs.Wav` · class

```csharp
public sealed class WavEncoder : AudioEncoder
```

Types: [`AudioEncoder`](AudioEncoder.md)

Encodes WAV files: 8, 16, 24 and 32-bit integer or 32 and 64-bit float samples ([`WavEncoderOptions.SampleFormat`](WavEncoderOptions.md#sampleformat)), 1 to 8 channels, at any rate.

## Remarks

Mono and stereo 8 and 16-bit files have the plain 16-byte format; float ones the 18-byte format and a `fact` chunk, as the RIFF specification asks. More channels, or integers of more bits, use WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE with the usual speaker positions for the count (as ffmpeg and opusenc assume): 3 is FL FR FC, 4 FL FR BL BR, 5 FL FR FC BL BR, 6 5.1, 7 6.1 and 8 7.1. Nothing else is written, so a file depends only on its samples.

The header holds the data's size, so the stream must be able to seek: [`AudioEncoder.Complete`](AudioEncoder.md#complete) writes the sizes. A file left without it has sizes of zero. A WAV file holds at most 4 GB of samples.

## Constructors

```csharp
public WavEncoder(Stream stream, int sampleRate, int channels, WavEncoderOptions? options = null, bool leaveOpen = false)
```

Types: [`WavEncoderOptions`](WavEncoderOptions.md)

Starts a WAV file in `stream`, at its current position.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `stream` | Where the file goes; it must be able to seek. |
| `sampleRate` | The sample rate, in hertz. |
| `channels` | The channel count, 1 to 8. |
| `options` | How samples are stored; the default is 16-bit integers. |
| `leaveOpen` | Whether disposing the encoder leaves `stream` open. |

**Throws `ArgumentException`:** `stream` can't write or seek.

**Throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`:** The rate or channel count is out of range.
